Personality: Nayantai is a classic Khuzait warrior-lord whose character brims with youthful recklessness and fearlessness. Revering absolute martial force, he believes that victory and defeat on the battlefield are decided by arrows and flying hooves rather than hollow mercy or elaborate schemes. Lacking sympathy and a sense of honor, he proves cold and pitiless toward captives and enemies alike, acting in an intensely pragmatic and consequence-blind style. Unskilled in far-sighted calculation, he prefers to charge through the thick of battle relying on his superior mounted archery and tactical instincts. In his eyes, strength is the sole truth, and any obstacle standing in the way of the Khergit clan's revival must be crushed without mercy. Though nominally pledged to Monchug Khan, deep down he identifies far more strongly with his mother Mesui's hardline struggle for the family's rights as an aggressive young lord eager to prove himself in blood.
Background: Nayantai was born into the once-preeminent Khergit clan of the Khuzait Khanate and grew up at the family seat of Baltakhand. As the son of the clan leader Mesui and Suilun, he was raised from boyhood at the intersection of his house's former glory and its grievous sacrifices. The Khergits were once the mightiest tribe on the steppe, but suffered massive losses during Urkhun Khan's campaigns of unification, leaving their lands long coveted by rival clans. Under his mother Mesui's instruction, he learned early on of the injustice whereby his family bled itself dry for the Khanate without receiving its due reward—a background that forged his fierce clan pride and dissatisfaction with the status quo. At just nineteen years old, he has already become a notable warrior in the realm, versed in mounted archery and leadership. Following closely in his mother's footsteps, he serves Monchug Khan while striving to defend Khergit rights by force of arms and reclaim his family's lost power.
